transcript:
Header: 2026-03-10 09:30 PDT | Duration: 65m | Attendees: Avery, Diego, Priya, Noah, Elena, Maya, Daniel, Samir, Lina, Tom, Rachel

Summary (auto): quick pre-launch sync and incident follow-up.

00:00 Avery: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, I want to run through the launch readiness checklist, high level timeline is next week for canary, full rollout two weeks after, um, quick heads up, legal and security are here to confirm gating items.
00:22 Maya: quick note, pls keep it tight on the SLA numbers -- execs asked for 95th perc p50 etc, we need the wording.
00:34 Diego: on SLA, we are tracking 95th under 220ms on p3 instances in staging right now, but we need prodlike bench to be confident. Noah, are we good to run the larger bench?
00:50 Noah: yes I'll kick off the 24-hour throughput run today, it's gonna test batching and the prefix K V cash warmup scenario, small chance the warmup increases lat a bit, i'll watch it.
01:04 Priya: also want to call out the incident last week where the worker pool OOMed during a large batch, root cause was the cache eviction miscalc and one of the predictor processes leaked memory. we've got mitigations but need the runbook updated.
01:21 Daniel: do we have a post-mortem doc somewhere?
01:26 Priya: yes it's in the incident folder, link in the chat, but the short version is memory leak + insufficient alerts on swap usage. we added an alert but need to tune thresholds.
01:39 Avery: good, action item to update runbook and alerts. Priya will own that.
01:46 Elena: i can prep the consumer-facing note for the beta customers, but we should finalize the SLO language first.
01:53 Tom: legal needs the data retention and logs section confirmed, especially around private deployments and KMS.
02:02 Lina: on KMS, the HSM path is ready, waiting on a small config flag for customer key rotation cadence, i'll add that to the security checklist.
02:14 Avery: great. let's walk the checklist -- first, telemetry: do we have token-level cost breakdown in console for the canary group?
02:26 Rachel: support has basic dashboards, not token-level yet, that's an enhancement we promised in the last kickoff.
02:34 Diego: it's important for early customers to see per-route cost. I'll allocate eng time but need to know priority.
02:42 Elena: mark as medium priority for canary; full token-level GA for broad launch.
02:51 Noah: perf note: when we enable continuous batching the 95th gets better but tail latency can spike in cold starts. we'll need to tune the batch timeout windows and pre-warm the KV cache for the canary.
03:06 Priya: adding the warmup step to deploy pipeline should be a standard job, no manual step. i'll draft the pipeline change and PR.
03:14 Diego: ok next, deployment plan: canary to 5% in us-west, monitor 24h, then regional expand. rollback policy is automatic fallback to smallest compatible variant - need to ensure models are pinned correctly.
03:28 Maya: what about dedicated vs hosted? are we launching hosted first?
03:32 Avery: yes hosted API + dedicated capacity for selected partners. Private on-prem is gated by legal/security sign-off.
03:42 Samir: infra ops note: provisioning for dedicated customers needs a steady-state pool; autoscale burst is fine but for initial customers we should reserve some capacity.
03:52 Noah: i'll add defaults for reserved-pool to terraform module, Diego will review.
04:00 Diego: also we must ensure compilation kernels are in place for the quantized variants; if not, fallbacks could increase cost.
04:12 Priya: monitoring, alerts: we need SLO burn rate alerts and a paged escalation that includes SE oncall and product lead for canary incidents.
04:24 Elena: can you enumerate the oncall rotation changes? we may need a temporary backfill for the first weekend after rollout.
04:33 Priya: yeah i'll coordinate with Samir to rotate oncall.
04:38 Daniel: incident review, any outstanding post-mortem actions?
04:42 Priya: a few: memory leak patch merged, but runway on the regression tests to catch similar leaks is still open, ETA end of week.
04:52 Noah: regression test will include stress with long-lived KV states, and we will also test the cold-start scenarios.
04:59 Avery: ask to include synthetic traces that simulate customer prompt distributions, not just uniform length.
05:08 Diego: noted. Bench plan: run small->medium->large and capture token-level cost and lat at each step. We'll publish a spreadsheet.
05:19 Elena: ok on comms: once Diego uploads bench, Elena will prepare readout for GTM and support; Avery will consolidate the sign-off matrix and send to execs.
05:28 Tom: legal needs a copy of the sign-off matrix, and the security checklist, before private customers are onboarded.
05:36 Lina: i'll attach the KMS config and the compliance notes (SOC2 bits) with the matrix.
05:44 Maya: timeline check, canary next tuesday 03/17?
05:49 Avery: target is 03/17 for initial canary, 03/31 for regional GA, contingent on benches and runbook completion.
05:58 Rachel: support readiness: create quick runbook for handling common customer issues and escalations. i can draft it once we have the runbook PR.
06:07 Priya: question on chaos testing - should we run a small chaos window during canary?
06:12 Daniel: yes but be cautious; if we run chaos we must limit blast radius and do it after 24h stable.
06:20 Diego: one more technical: kernel selection for quantized models, if the optimized kernel fails we shouldn't silently use a slower path without flagging it as a regression. add a metric for kernel fallback.
06:33 Noah: can do, will add metric and an alert when fallback rate exceeds 1%.
06:40 Avery: ok wrap up - recap action items... (recap of items follows)
06:52 Avery: quick note, transcription is rough, there are a few garbled words in the transcript, see the PR for the incident doc.
06:58 Daniel: thanks all, see you on the bench check-in later this week.
07:05 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains some errors: 'KV cache' occasionally transcribed as 'K V cash', 'Redwood Optimize' shows up as 'Redwood Optima' in one place; speaker overlaps around 03:06.
